title: Indian GM Pranesh M Wins Prestigious Kanizsa Open 2026 in Hungary
excerpt: The 19-year-old from Tamil Nadu defeated Germany's Vadim Petrovskiy in the final round to claim the Group A title at one of Central Europe's strongest open chess tournaments.
body:
• Indian Grandmaster Pranesh M, 19, won the Kanizsa Open 2026 in Nagykanizsa, Hungary, finishing with 7 points from 9 rounds.
  • Ranked 44th in the world by FIDE, Pranesh defeated Germany's Vadim Petrovskiy in the decisive final round on August 23.
  • The tournament attracted 226 players with a Tournament Average Rating above 2605, making it one of Central Europe's strongest open events.
  • The Indian Embassy in Hungary hailed his victory, calling the country a "happy hunting ground for Indian chess."

India's 19-year-old Grandmaster Pranesh M clinched the Group A title at the prestigious Kanizsa Open 2026 in Nagykanizsa, Hungary, capping a dominant nine-round performance in one of Central Europe's most competitive open chess tournaments.

Pranesh, whose full name is Pranesh Munirethinam, defeated Germany's Vadim Petrovskiy with the white pieces in the ninth and final round on Sunday, August 23, to seal the championship. He finished with 7 points from 9 games, sharing the top tally with three other competitors but prevailing on tiebreaks.

A Strong Field Falls to India's Rising Star

The Kanizsa Open, held from August 15 to 23, drew 226 players and carried a Tournament Average Rating exceeding 2605 — a benchmark that places it among the elite tier of European open tournaments. Israel's Or Bronstein finished as runner-up, while Ukrainian veteran Andrei Volokitin took third place.

Pranesh, who hails from Karaikudi in Tamil Nadu, currently holds a FIDE rating of 2673 and sits at 44th in the August 2026 world rankings. At just 19, he has already established himself as a fixture among the world's top 50 players and one of the brightest talents in India's formidable chess pipeline.

India's Embassy Celebrates

The Indian Embassy in Hungary was quick to celebrate the victory. In a post on X, the embassy wrote: "Meet the new Indian Chess Champion!! Pranesh M. Huge Congratulations to Indian Grandmaster Pranesh M on his brilliant victory at the prestigious Kanizsa Open 2026 in Nagykanizsa, Hungary!"

"After a thrilling 9th round, Pranesh secured the top spot in one of Central Europe's most competitive open tournaments. We are incredibly proud to see Indian talent shining so brightly on the global stage. Hungary continues to be a happy hunting ground for Indian Chess."

— Indian Embassy in Hungary (@IndiaInHungary), August 23, 2026

A Summer of Dominance

The Kanizsa Open victory caps an extraordinary summer for Pranesh. Earlier in August, he dominated the Chess.com 3|0 Thursday blitz event on August 6, scoring 10.5 out of 11 — tying the record for the most dominant performance in the tournament's history. He defeated multiple top-ranked opponents including GMs Alexey Sarana, Vladimir Fedoseev, and Jeffery Xiong during that run.

In June, Pranesh won the Freestyle Friday Championship on Chess.com and earned automatic qualification for the Chess.com Open Playoffs. He also competed in the 2026 Quantbox Chennai Grand Masters, having earned his spot by winning the 2025 Challengers section of the same event — a tournament that previously launched world champion Gukesh Dommaraju's path to the Candidates.

India's Chess Conveyor Belt

Pranesh's victory underscores the depth of India's chess talent pipeline at a time when the country stands at the pinnacle of the sport. Gukesh became the youngest-ever world chess champion in late 2024 at age 18, while players like Arjun Erigaisi, Nihal Sarin, and R. Praggnanandhaa continue to hold top-20 world rankings.

For the Indian diaspora, the sustained success of Indian chess players at the highest levels has become a familiar source of pride. The embassy's reference to Hungary as a "happy hunting ground" reflects a broader trend: Indian grandmasters have increasingly dominated European open tournaments, leveraging these events to gain rating points and international exposure.

What's Next

Pranesh's strong run of form positions him well for the remainder of the 2026 competitive season. With a growing world ranking and a proven ability to deliver in high-pressure classical and blitz formats, the Tamil Nadu native is expected to feature prominently in upcoming FIDE Circuit events and continue his push toward the world's top 30.
